_note: Shared prompt blocks for p4-char-concept-cb1. code/run_sheets_p4-char-concept-cb1.py assembles: layout + identity_lock + 'Character: ' + character_en + ' Costume: ' + costume visual_en (verbatim from bible/costumes.json) + ' Style: ' + style.json style_fragment_ui (verbatim, read at run time) + ' ' + recap. Negative = style.json negative_prompt_en (+ negative_prompt_waking_addon_en for waking-world subjects) + ', ' + negative_layout_addon. The exact submitted strings are written back into each character's prompts.json.

human.layout: Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The sheet looks like four production photographs mounted side by side on one board: the image is divided by three thin vertical gaps into three narrow full-height panels on the left and one wide panel on the right. Panel 1: full-body front view, standing naturally, facing the camera. Panel 2: full-body side profile view facing right. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4 (right column): large head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera or a slight three-quarter turn, the face sharp and clear. Each full-body view shows the whole figure from the top of the head to the soles of the shoes with clear space above and below, a small patch of floor and a soft contact shadow under the feet; any part cut off by a panel edge makes the sheet invalid. Plain seamless warm light-grey studio backdrop in every panel, soft even light, no scenery.
human.identity_lock: Identity lock: one and the same person in all four panels, with the same face, hair, build and costume; exactly one figure per panel; no duplicated or extra figures.
human.recap: Layout recap (highest priority): four separate photographic panels side by side on one sheet: front, side profile, back, head-and-shoulders close-up; plain studio backdrop; never one single full-bleed picture.

animal.layout: Four-panel creature reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views of the animal (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head close-up filling the right column; the exact same animal, markings and proportions in every panel; plain background. The sheet looks like four production photographs mounted side by side on one board: the image is divided by three thin vertical gaps into three narrow full-height panels on the left and one wide panel on the right; each panel is its own small photograph and the animal is scaled to fit completely inside each narrow panel. Panel 1: full-body front view, facing the camera. Panel 2: full-body side profile view facing right. Panel 3: full-body back view. Panel 4 (right column): large close-up of the head and chest, facing the camera or a slight three-quarter turn, eyes, nose and whiskers sharp. Macro studio photography at the animal's own eye level: in each full-body view the whole animal, including the ears, feet and the full tail, sits inside the panel with clear space around it, on a small patch of floor with a soft contact shadow. Plain seamless warm light-grey studio backdrop in every panel, soft even light, no scenery, no props other than those named below.
animal.identity_lock: Identity lock: one and the same individual animal in all four panels, with identical fur or scale pattern, markings, eye colour and build; exactly one animal per panel; no duplicated or extra animals.
animal.recap: Layout recap (highest priority): four separate photographic panels side by side on one sheet: front, side profile, back, head close-up; plain studio backdrop; never one single full-bleed picture; a real photographed animal, not a cartoon.

negative_layout_addon: single full-bleed illustration, one single panel, scenery background, crowd, text labels
